title: One store. Too many jobs.
captions: You started a store.
Website. Listings. Ads. Reports. The work piles up.
Who connects it? You do.
notes: Open on the merchant, not on AI. The problem is coordination: a small merchant has to carry the same product facts across separate tools and make spending decisions from separate reports. This is a problem hypothesis, not a quantified market finding.

title: One connected workspace.
captions: Meet RunMyStore. One connected workspace.
From product to storefront. From creative to campaign. With you in control.
notes: Position RunMyStore as the connected merchant workspace. Its central value is that product context and approvals travel through the workflow. The AI actions are simulated for this hackathon UI prototype.

title: Start with the product truth.
captions: Start with a product and the facts you know.
Prepare descriptions, images and search metadata.
Review the listing before it moves downstream.
notes: Catalog Studio supports product fields, SKU validation, image input and listing preparation. The demo uses prepared output; it does not infer factual claims from a photograph. Unknown material or dimensions must be supplied by the merchant. The approved artifact is reusable downstream.

title: A storefront that feels like you.
captions: Build a storefront around the same catalog.
Edit sections, refine your brand, check mobile.
Then review and publish your demo.
notes: Use Website Builder in the live demo: edit the hero and sections, preview desktop or mobile, and review the draft. Publication creates an immutable local demo snapshot, not a public live store. Approved catalog products are available to this builder.

title: One product. Three introductions.
captions: Turn that product into ad concepts.
Compare variations for Meta, Google and TikTok.
Edit the copy. Save a creative. Attach it to a campaign.
notes: The UI creates prepared editable concepts tied to the selected catalog product, with platform previews and a versioned creative library. These visuals illustrate concept preparation, not live ads. Static artwork and carousel cards can export as PNG; generated video is currently a storyboard.

title: See what the campaign is doing.
captions: Track spend, revenue and purchases together.
See campaign status and compare channels.
Seeded demo figures illustrate the decisions a merchant needs to make.
notes: All numbers are October 1–24, 2026 fixtures from the app: $31,920 attributed revenue, $9,000 ad spend, 399 purchases. ROAS is 31,920 divided by 9,000, rounded to 3.55. This is not company traction, a causal lift claim, or a forecast. New demo campaigns begin with zero history; next-day events are simulated.

title: Move the money. Keep the limit.
captions: Move $500 from Meta and $300 from TikTok to Google.
The $12,000 monthly cap stays fixed.
You review the proposal and approve the change.
notes: This is the exact planning scenario in the app. Meta moves from $6,000 to $5,500; Google from $3,600 to $4,400; TikTok from $2,400 to $2,100. The total stays at $12,000. The recommendation responds to seeded pacing, not a proven performance optimization. Show Review, then Approve & apply, then the decision journal.

title: Agentic by design. Human by decision.
captions: The intended orchestration layer: AgenticOrg by Pine Labs.
Shared context. Specialist roles. Approval before action.
Today the connected UI uses mock data. Agent execution is simulated.
notes: Be explicit with judges: AgenticOrg is a proposed integration; current role handoffs are simulated. Proposed flow: a request carries shared product/catalog context; specialists prepare artifacts; the operator presents a diff; a merchant approves; a scoped tool executes and records a receipt. Real AgenticOrg, model and external provider calls remain next steps, not completed features.

title: You run the business.
captions: You run the business. RunMyStore runs the store.
Let’s walk through the prototype: one product, one campaign, one approved decision.
notes: Switch to the live prototype. Start in Catalog Studio and open the draft mug. Confirm material, prepare and approve the listing. Show Website Builder, then Ad Studio, attach a saved creative to a draft campaign, and close by reviewing the budget recommendation. State that all external actions are simulated.
